gates.gate: a real substantive application, not a demo or tutorial scaffold
gates.evidence: 558 TypeScript files, 80 component templates and 113 SCSS files under src, organised into 17 feature domains (tasks, time-tracking, project, config, worklog, metric, pomodoro, reminder, note, bookmark, attachment, issue, google, imex, planning-mode, procrastination, task-repeat-cfg) plus core, core-ui, pages, root-store, ui and util layers. Ten routed pages. An ngrx 8 root store with effects, entity and data. A published desktop product with its own domain, not a sample.
gates.detail: This is the largest single-application Angular fixture admitted to the corpus so far.

gates.evidence: @angular/core ^8.2.6 with the whole platform at ^8.2.x, @angular/cli ^8.3.4, @angular-devkit/build-angular pinned exactly at 0.803.4, typescript ~3.5.3, ngrx 8. `enableIvy` appears in zero of the 967 blobs, and Angular 8.2 defaults to ViewEngine, so the AOT production build that succeeded compiled through ViewEngine.
gates.eraGapFilled: the pre-Ivy ViewEngine cell the Angular cohort was missing

gates.evidence: Annotated tag v2.13.15 dated 2019-12-05T21:01:13Z; commit 2943c5c4 committed and authored the same instant. Inside the required revision window 2018-01-01 through 2021-12-31.

gates.gate: at least three substantive journeys plausible
journeys: task create / edit — the tasks feature over the ngrx store, entered from the work-view page
task drag reorder — ng2-dragula 2.1.1 wired through the task list components
time tracking start / stop — the time-tracking feature with its own store slice and the worklog page
project switch — the project feature plus the projects and project-settings pages
settings — the config page over @ngx-formly 5 schema-driven forms
dark theme — angular-material-css-vars 0.1.6 driving Material theming through CSS custom properties
keyboard shortcuts — a configurable shortcut layer in the config surface
import / export — the imex feature, backed by localforage and lz-string compression
gates.backendEvidence: State lives in src/app/core/persistence over localforage and browser local storage (persistence.service.ts, database.service.ts, local-storage.ts). No API base URL is configured for the core flow and no server is needed to exercise the journeys above.

recordedNonMaskingFacts.detail: @angular/service-worker 8.2.x with ngsw-config.json; the production build emits ngsw-worker.js, ngsw.json and safety-worker.js. Its externalAssets group prefetches https://fonts.googleapis.com/** and https://fonts.gstatic.com/**.
recordedNonMaskingFacts.disposition: recorded, not disabled. Establishes the non-masking precedent for later units: a service-worker-free variant must be a labeled deviation, never the unlabeled baseline.

recordedNonMaskingFacts.detail: tsconfig.worker.json is wired into the browser builder via webWorkerTsConfig. Two application workers compile and emit: lz (lz-string compression) and reminder.
recordedNonMaskingFacts.disposition: recorded and exercised — both emitted in the green production build.

recordedNonMaskingFacts.detail: An electron/ directory (15 TypeScript modules: main, main-window, jira, google-auth, backup, dbus, lockscreen, indicator, git-log and others), electron 6.1.5, electron-builder 22.2.0, tsconfig-electron.json, electron-builder.yaml and a build/ asset tree. package.json `main` points at ./electron/main.js and the `start` script launches Electron, not the browser.
recordedNonMaskingFacts.disposition: out of build scope for this unit and never invoked. Recorded so that later units know the repository's default entry point is the desktop shell, and that `yarn start` is not a web dev server — `startFrontend` is.

recordedNonMaskingFacts.fact: optional third-party integrations, off by default
recordedNonMaskingFacts.detail: Jira (jira-client-fork, jira.const.ts declares isEnabled: false), Google Drive/Sheets sync (googleapis 40, toggled off until a user enables it) and GitHub issue import.
recordedNonMaskingFacts.disposition: recorded with egress destinations below for witness blocking.

egressDestinationsForWitnessBlocking.purpose: Destinations any later browser-witness unit must block or stub, so that exercising this fixture cannot reach third-party hosts.

unconditionalAtPageLoad.severity: fires on every page load with no user action and no setting to turn it off

unconditionalAtPageLoad.source: the font files the above stylesheet references, plus the ngsw externalAssets prefetch group

conditionalOnUserEnablingAnIntegration.source: the Jira integration; the host is supplied by the user, so no fixed destination can be allowlisted in advance

egressDestinationsForWitnessBlocking.notEgress: confluence.atlassian.com, drsoph.com, nytimes.com, chrome.google.com, developers.google.com and similar appear only as documentation and help links in template markup. They are navigation targets a user could click, not requests the application issues.
egressDestinationsForWitnessBlocking.comparisonToPriorLanes: Unlike the jira-clone lane, this fixture hard-codes no Sentry DSN and no Google Analytics id. Nothing reports to an upstream author's telemetry property at bootstrap. The only unconditional third-party traffic is Google Fonts.
